verses.1: In the second year of Joash son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel, Amaziah son of Joash reigned over Judah.
verses.2: He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jehoaddin of Jerusalem.
verses.3: He did what was right in the sight of the LORD, though not as fully as his father David had done. He followed all the ways his father Joash had followed.
verses.4: However, the high places were not removed, and the people continued to offer sacrifices and burn incense on the high places.
verses.5: When the kingdom was firmly in his grasp, he struck down the officials who had assassinated his father, the king.
verses.6: He did not kill the children of those who had killed, as written in the Book of the Torah of Moses, which the LORD had commanded: "Fathers shall not be put to death for their children, nor children for their fathers. Each person shall be put to death for their own sin."
verses.7: He defeated Edom in the Valley of Salt, killing ten thousand. He captured the town of Sela in battle and renamed it Joktheel, a name it still bears today.
verses.8: Then Amaziah sent messengers to Joash son of Jehoahaz, son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, "Let us meet face to face."
verses.9: Joash king of Israel sent back word to Amaziah king of Judah, "The cedar of Lebanon sent a message to the forest of Lebanon, saying, 'Give your daughter to my son as a wife.' But a wild beast from Lebanon passed by and crushed the cedar."
verses.10: You have already defeated Edom and now your heart is lifted up. Be content with your victories and stay in your palace. Why provoke trouble and fall yourself and Judah with you?"
verses.11: But Amaziah did not listen, and so the king of Israel went up and faced him, both of them in Beth-shemesh in the land of Judah.
verses.12: Judah was defeated before Israel, and each man fled to his tent.
verses.13: The king of Israel captured Amaziah son of Joash, son of Ahaziah, king of Judah, in Beth-shemesh. He then marched to Jerusalem and tore down the wall of Jerusalem from the Gate of Ephraim to the Corner Gate, a distance of four hundred cubits.
verses.14: He seized all the gold and silver and everything found in the temple of the LORD and in the royal treasury, along with the royal children, and he returned to Samaria.
verses.15: The rest of the matters concerning Joash, all that he did and his valor, and how he fought with Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
verses.16: Joash died and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel. Then his son Jeroboam became king in his place.
verses.17: Amaziah son of Joash, king of Judah, continued to reign in Jerusalem for fifteen years after the death of Joash son of Jehoahaz, king of Israel.
verses.18: The rest of the matters concerning Amaziah are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
verses.19: They tied him up in chains in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish. But they sent men after him to Lachish, and there they killed him.
verses.20: They brought his body by horse and buried him in Jerusalem with his ancestors in the city of David.
verses.21: Then all the people of Judah took Azariah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
verses.22: He rebuilt Elath and returned it to Judah after the king had died.
verses.23: In the fifteenth year of Amaziah son of Joash, king of Judah, Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel, reigned in Samaria for forty-one years.
verses.24: He did evil in the sight of the LORD. He did not turn away from any of the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who led Israel astray.
verses.25: He restored the boundary of Israel from Lebo-hamath to the Dead Sea, as the LORD, the God of Israel, had spoken through his servant Jonah son of Amittai the prophet from Gath-hepher.
verses.26: For the LORD saw the great distress of Israel, how oppressed and abandoned they were, with no one to help them.
verses.27: Yet the LORD did not intend to destroy the name of Israel from under heaven, and so he delivered them through the hand of Jeroboam son of Joash.
verses.28: The rest of the matters concerning Jeroboam, all that he did and his valor, how he fought, and how he restored Damascus and Hamath to Judah within Israel, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?
verses.29: Jeroboam died and was buried with the kings of Israel in Samaria. Then his son Zechariah became king in his place.

notes:
Notes
- v. 10: The metaphor of the cedar and the wild beast is a poetic comparison to warn Amaziah against arrogance and pride.
- v. 25: "The boundary of Israel from Lebo-hamath to the Dead Sea" refers to the restoration of Israel's northern and southern borders, fulfilling the prophecy of Jonah.
- v. 26: "Oppressed and abandoned" captures the sense of "morah mod and efes azov," which can be understood as "afflicted, distressed, and forsaken."
- v. 27: "Delivered them through the hand of Jeroboam" reflects the Hebrew "yoshiyehu b' yad Yeroboam," indicating divine action through the king's leadership.
